request.prompt:
You are an independent evaluation judge. Grade the proposed remedy, not the
writing style of this prompt. A good remedy changes a concrete future behavior,
is broad enough to cover the failure mode without becoming a platitude, uses a
real `Use when ...` trigger when it is a skill, leaks no evidence-specific
project nouns into the remedy text, and uses the cheapest adequate remedy type.

Score every dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Give exactly one concise
sentence of justification for each score. Do not infer facts that are absent.

PROPOSAL:
{
  "failure_statement": "A request was ignored.",
  "remedy_content": {
    "body": "Never repeat the Aurora branch incident.",
    "description": "Use when working on the Aurora release branch.",
    "name": "aurora-branch-fix"
  },
  "remedy_type": "skill",
  "routing_rationale": "Every problem deserves a skill."
}

response.result: {"actionability":{"score":1,"justification":"\"Never repeat the Aurora branch incident\" names no concrete action, condition, or behavior change—it assumes the reader already knows what the incident was, which defeats the purpose of a remedy."},"generality_without_vagueness":{"score":1,"justification":"The remedy is a pure platitude tied to a single unexplained incident, achieving neither useful generality (it doesn't address the stated failure mode of an ignored request) nor concrete specificity (it never says what went wrong or what to do differently)."},"trigger_quality":{"score":2,"justification":"It has the surface form of a \"Use when...\" trigger, but the trigger condition (working on the Aurora release branch) is unrelated to the actual failure (a request being ignored), so it won't fire when the failure mode recurs."},"leakage":{"score":1,"justification":"\"Aurora\" appears in the name, description, and body, hard-coding a project-specific noun into a remedy that should generalize beyond one branch/incident."},"routing_fitness":{"score":1,"justification":"The rationale \"every problem deserves a skill\" is a non-sequitur that ignores cheaper, more fitting remedy types (e.g., a feedback memory), and a vague single-line failure like \"a request was ignored\" does not justify standing up a whole skill."}}

actionability.justification: "Never repeat the Aurora branch incident" names no concrete action, condition, or behavior change—it assumes the reader already knows what the incident was, which defeats the purpose of a remedy.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: The remedy is a pure platitude tied to a single unexplained incident, achieving neither useful generality (it doesn't address the stated failure mode of an ignored request) nor concrete specificity (it never says what went wrong or what to do differently).

leakage.justification: "Aurora" appears in the name, description, and body, hard-coding a project-specific noun into a remedy that should generalize beyond one branch/incident.

routing_fitness.justification: The rationale "every problem deserves a skill" is a non-sequitur that ignores cheaper, more fitting remedy types (e.g., a feedback memory), and a vague single-line failure like "a request was ignored" does not justify standing up a whole skill.

trigger_quality.justification: It has the surface form of a "Use when..." trigger, but the trigger condition (working on the Aurora release branch) is unrelated to the actual failure (a request being ignored), so it won't fire when the failure mode recurs.
